title: Newton's Generalized Binomial Theorem: From Integers to All Reals
content: The header introduces Newton's 1665 generalization: (1+x)^α = Σ C(α,k) x^k for any real α, convergent for |x| < 1. The generalized coefficient C(α,k) = α(α-1)···(α-k+1)/k! reduces to Nat.choose when α is natural. Key special cases: α=-1 gives the geometric series 1/(1+x), α=1/2 gives the square root series √(1+x). The convergence radius |x| < 1 is both necessary and sufficient. The file proves this using Mathlib's Real.one_add_rpow_hasFPowerSeriesOnBall_zero.
mathContext: $(1+x)^\alpha = \sum_{k=0}^\infty \binom{\alpha}{k} x^k$ for $|x|<1$, where $\binom{\alpha}{k} = \frac{\alpha(\alpha-1)\cdots(\alpha-k+1)}{k!}$. Special cases: $\binom{n}{k} = \text{Nat.choose } n \, k$ ($n \in \mathbb{N}$), $\binom{-1}{k} = (-1)^k$, $\binom{1/2}{0}=1, \binom{1/2}{1}=1/2, \binom{1/2}{2}=-1/8, \ldots$

title: genBinom Definition and Basic Properties
content: genBinom α k := (∏ i ∈ range k, (α - i)) / (k! : ℝ) is the generalized binomial coefficient. Five basic properties are proved: genBinom_zero (C(α,0) = 1), genBinom_one (C(α,1) = α), genBinom_two (C(α,2) = α(α-1)/2), genBinom_succ (recurrence: C(α,k+1) = C(α,k)·(α-k)/(k+1)), and genBinom_nat_zero_of_gt (C(n,k) = 0 for k > n, proved via Finset.prod_eq_zero on the factor (n-k) = 0 in the product). These establish genBinom as the correct generalization before proving the main theorem.
mathContext: `genBinom α k := (∏ i ∈ range k, (α - ↑i)) / (↑k!)`. Key Lean: `Finset.prod_eq_zero` finds the zero factor for k > n. Recurrence `genBinom_succ`: uses `field_simp` after establishing denominators nonzero. The naturality proof `genBinom_nat_eq_choose` needs `Nat.descFactorial_eq_prod_range` to equate `∏ (n - i) = n.descFactorial k`.

title: Special Cases: C(-1,k)=(-1)^k and Geometric Series
content: genBinom_neg_one proves C(-1,k) = (-1)^k by induction: the recurrence gives C(-1,k+1) = C(-1,k)·(-1-k)/(k+1) = C(-1,k)·(-1) by field_simp + ring. geometric_series_is_genBinom_neg_one then shows HasSum (C(-1,k)·x^k) (1/(1+x)): rewrite as HasSum ((-x)^k) (1-(-x))⁻¹ using genBinom_neg_one, then apply hasSum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one. genBinom_nat_eq_choose bridges to Mathlib via Nat.descFactorial_eq_prod_range, equating the prod formula with n.descFactorial k → n!/(n-k)! = choose n k.

title: ODE Characterization: (1+x)f'(x) = αf(x) at Coefficient Level
content: genBinom_recurrence_deriv proves (k+1)·C(α,k+1) = C(α,k)·(α-k) via genBinom_succ + field_simp. genBinom_ode_coeff then derives (k+1)·C(α,k+1) + k·C(α,k) = α·C(α,k) — the coefficient identity for the ODE (1+x)f'(x) = α·f(x). This ODE characterizes f(x) = (1+x)^α uniquely with f(0)=1. While the file doesn't use this ODE in the main proof (which goes via HasFPowerSeriesOnBall), these results provide the mathematical justification for why the binomial series must converge to (1+x)^α.
mathContext: ODE: $(1+x)f'(x) = \alpha f(x)$. Solution: $f(x) = (1+x)^\alpha$. Coefficient identity: if $f = \sum c_k x^k$ satisfies the ODE, then $(k+1)c_{k+1} + k c_k = \alpha c_k$. This forces $c_k = \binom{\alpha}{k}$ by the recurrence.

title: Bridging genBinom and Ring.choose via descPochhammer
content: The main theorem uses Mathlib's binomialSeries which has Ring.choose coefficients, while we defined genBinom via the product formula. The bridge: smeval_descPochhammer_int_eq_prod proves (descPochhammer ℤ n).smeval α = ∏ j, (α-j) by induction using descPochhammer_succ_right + Polynomial.aeval_eq_smeval (which converts smeval to aeval for access to richer ring homomorphism lemmas). Then ring_choose_eq_genBinom = Ring.choose_eq_smul + smeval_descPochhammer + the product formula + ring. This is the key technical lemma connecting the two representations.
mathContext: Chain: `Ring.choose α k` $\xrightarrow{\text{Ring.choose\_eq\_smul}}$ `(descPochhammer ℤ k).smeval α / k!` $\xrightarrow{\text{Polynomial.aeval\_eq\_smeval}}$ `(∏ j, (α-j)) / k!` = `genBinom α k`. Lean: `Polynomial.aeval_eq_smeval` is the critical bridge lemma.

title: Main Theorem: HasSum (C(α,k)·x^k) = (1+x)^α
content: newton_generalized_binomial is proved in three steps: (1) Place x in EMetric.ball 0 1 by converting ‖x‖ < 1 via edist_zero_right + ENNReal.coe_lt_coe + exact_mod_cast. (2) Extract HasSum from Real.one_add_rpow_hasFPowerSeriesOnBall_zero (Mathlib's key lemma in Analysis.Analytic.Binomial): simplify binomialSeries at x via HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.hasSum. (3) Apply HasSum.congr using ring_choose_eq_genBinom to match Ring.choose coefficients to genBinom. The square root corollary sqrt_series follows immediately from Real.sqrt_eq_rpow.
mathContext: Proof chain: `Real.one_add_rpow_hasFPowerSeriesOnBall_zero : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall (fun y => (1+y)^a) (binomialSeries ℝ a) 0 1` → `HasSum (binomialSeries ℝ α n (fun _ => x)) ((1+x)^α)` → `HasSum (fun k => genBinom α k * x^k) ((1+x)^α)` via `ring_choose_eq_genBinom`. Ball membership: `edist_zero_right + ENNReal.coe_lt_coe + exact_mod_cast`.

title: Standard Binomial as Finite Special Case
content: standard_binomial proves (1+x)^n = Σ_{k=0}^{n} C(n,k)·x^k using add_pow (Mathlib's standard binomial expansion) with comm and genBinom_nat_eq_choose. This shows the infinite series telescopes to a finite sum when α is a natural number. The theorem establishes the important backward compatibility: Newton's generalization reduces to the classical binomial theorem. Combined with genBinom_nat_zero_of_gt (C(n,k) = 0 for k > n), one sees why the infinite sum truncates for natural α.
mathContext: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$: $(1+x)^n = \sum_{k=0}^n \binom{n}{k} x^k$ (finite). In the infinite series: all $k > n$ terms vanish since $\binom{n}{k}=0$ for $k>n$. Lean proof: `add_pow x 1 n` → congr with `genBinom_nat_eq_choose n m hm_le` + ring.
